transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-02 15:00 UTC
Duration: 50 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Khan (Redwood AE), Marco Lin (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Redwood CSM), Daniel Park (CTO, Boreal), Marta Ruiz (Platform Engineer), Liam O'Neill (SRE)

Auto-summary: quick check of pilot metrics, go-live playbook walkthrough, assign owners for runbooks and monitoring. Some network/VPC peering clarifications and a perf run planned.

00:00 - Aisha: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we wanted to use this slot to walk through the pilot transition playbook — make sure the canary steps and rollback are clear and assign owners. how's everyone doing?
00:18 - Daniel: good thanks, couple of things on our side, we saw that the pilot's error rate dropped after the quant patch but latency was a touch higher than we expected in the long tail.
00:30 - Marco: yeah that's consistent with the earlier run; when we bumped batch size for throughput the p95 shifted. we can tweak batching and enable prefix cache for repeated requests to recover p95 while keeping cost down, mm.
00:53 - Marta: quick clarification, when you say prefix cache do we need to open any additional ports on the peered VPC or is that all application layer?
01:07 - Marco: mostly app layer; the KV cache sits inside the runtime on the same pod so no extra inbound from your side. only network piece is the peering for model artifacts pulls during warmups, which is small but yes we should list that in the runbook.
01:30 - Liam: okay noted, also on the security side are we going to use customer KMS or Redwood-managed key for the dedicated nodes during the pilot? this affects key rotation steps in the runbook.
01:45 - Aisha: we flagged that earlier — Boreal asked for KMS keys in customer account. Marco, are there any gotchas with that for the ded... the Redwood Dedicated setup? (laughs)
01:56 - Marco: yeah, small naming slip there — it should be Redwood Dedicated, but from the infra side using customer KMS is supported. we do need one IAM role assumption step and we'll add the exact policy snippet to the playbook.
02:18 - Daniel: great, can you paste that into the shared doc? we've had issues with overly-broad roles in other pilots.
02:27 - Marco: will do, I'll paste a least-privilege example.
02:33 - Priya: Action item: we'll also add the compliance checklist around audit logs and retention so your security folks can tick boxes during the run.
02:43 - Marta: perfect. back to the rollout — what are you recommending for the canary percentages? last call mentioned 5/25/100 but I'd rather avoid tiny steps if we're using auto-scaling.
02:59 - Marco: given your traffic profile (burstier afternoons), we recommend a three-step: 10% for 4 hours with close SLO checks, 50% for 12 hours with load-run validation, then 100% for canary cutover. the reason is noise at 5% can be misleading for error budgets on small samples.
03:25 - Daniel: makes sense. what monitoring do you want us to set up? we already have Datadog and a basic synthetic.
03:33 - Marco: perfect — two things: (1) realtime token-level latency traces for p50/p95/p99 from Redwood's tracing hook; (2) alert on error-rate > 0.5% sustained for 5 minutes AND p95 > 1200ms. we'll provide the Datadog dashboards and the alert definitions.
03:56 - Liam: for paging, if both error-rate and p95 fire, we want an automatic page to the on-call; if just p95 degrades but error-rate ok, we'll page during business hours only. is that configurable?
04:11 - Aisha: yes, that's in the playbook as conditional paging. we'll include how to wire alerts to your Opsgenie/Slack channels.
04:20 - Daniel: ok good.
04:24 - Marco: quick note on canary failure modes: if model variant shows hallucinations above baseline, we prefer immediate rollback to previous model and throttle to 0% for the canary. the playbook includes a rapid-assess checklist: sample prompts, eval harness run, and manual sign-off.
04:45 - Marta: do you have an automated A/B metric we can rely on, or is it manual comparison?
04:52 - Marco: we can do automated reranking metrics and quality counters if you ingest reference prompts. for the pilot we recommend a hybrid: automated checks for token-level regressions and a small human review panel for semantic drift.
05:10 - Daniel: who's responsible for the human review?
05:15 - Priya: typically customers provide SMEs; Redwood can help recruit a couple of reviewers if needed for the initial window. we'll note that as an option.
05:26 - Aisha: let's talk cutover sequencing — database migrations or schema changes?
05:31 - Marta: no DB schema changes for now; just config toggles and route weights. one concern is session affinity during canary; our gateway uses sticky sessions. could that cause split-brain on the kv cache?
05:47 - Marco: session stickiness could bias results. we recommend cookie-less routing for the canary slice or use consistent hashing on request id. we'll add a config snippet for Envoy and for nginx.
06:05 - Liam: noted. also we need to ensure that our observability instrumentation tags requests with internal customer ids to reconcile billing and SLOs. is that already supported?
06:17 - Marco: yes, we support custom token tags; we'll include the header names and example payloads in the runbook. small chance of header name collisions, so please confirm which header you'll use.
06:32 - Daniel: we'll use X-Boreal-ReqID, we'll add that to the doc.
06:36 - Aisha: great. now on rollback timing, how long do you recommend waiting at each canary step before rollback?
06:42 - Marco: for our recommended 10%/50%/100% pattern: 10% wait 4 hours with continuous checks; if no alerts and perf stable then move to 50% and run a short stress ramp for 2 hours, then 12 hours steady before final. the playbook sets hard-time windows and a manual approval gate at 50%.
07:06 - Marta: can we shorten the 12 hours to 4 overnight if things look green and our SRE approves?
07:14 - Marco: we can, but keep in mind the long-tail p99 may not surface in 4 hours depending on traffic variance. if you're comfortable, we can add a conditional clause to the playbook for low-traffic windows.
07:28 - Daniel: moving on — can we go over the rollback steps quickly? I want to ensure the db of config is correct.
07:35 - Marco: sure. rollback is: (1) instantly shift weight to previous model variant via routing (we have API to set weights), (2) clear KV cache to avoid stale prefixes, (3) redeploy if needed, (4) run quick smoke tests and notify stakeholders. we'll paste CLI snippets and console steps in the playbook.
07:56 - Priya: add an incident severity classification: Sev1 for error-rate > 1% or sustained outage, Sev2 for p95 spike > 2x baseline, Sev3 for degradation without immediate customer impact.
08:12 - Liam: that classification works. we also want postmortem timeline — within 48 hours for Sev1.
08:18 - Priya: yes we'll include that.
08:21 - Daniel: on the topic of costs, if we autoscale dedicated nodes for canary we'll see some bursty billing. any recommendations to bound spend?
08:33 - Marco: two levers: set a hard capacity cap on the GPU pool for the pilot and use smaller quantized model variant for canary traffic (we have quant profiles). Redwood Optimize can recommend a mix based on your token distribution; we'll run that offline and share the recommendation.
08:55 - Marta: please share the cost delta for small vs medium quant profiles, that's useful for our finance folks.
09:02 - Aisha: action item — Marco to run Optimize job and attach cost delta table.
09:09 - Marco: will do.
09:12 - Daniel: last engineering question — private deployment vs dedicated — for pilot we want dedicated with VPC peering but no private control plane yet, correct?
09:23 - Aisha: correct, pilot uses Redwood Dedicated with VPC peering into your account. Private control plane is a later step for production if needed.
09:33 - Marta: ok good.
09:36 - Liam: one more ask — can you add a quick troubleshooting cheat-sheet for high-latency? my on-call will appreciate top-5 checks.
09:46 - Marco: yep, top-5 checks will be added: (1) check GPU utilization & queue length, (2) examine KV cache hit-rate, (3) inspect model variant and recent rollouts, (4) check network egress/ingress latencies, (5) validate tokenization corner-cases.
10:04 - Daniel: awesome.
10:09 - Aisha: ok let's recap next steps — we'll share an updated playbook that includes the KMS snippet, Envoy config, Datadog alert queries, and rollback CLI snippets. Marco will run the perf load test at 10% traffic next week and share numbers. Marta will add peering details and confirm header names. Liam will define the alert paging policy.
10:36 - Marta: I will also invite our security lead to the shared doc for the SOC2 and audit log retention checklist.
10:46 - Priya: timeline notes: we aim to start canary next week pending perf run, so please try to close the playbook items by 2025-07-08 so rollout target remains July 10th.
10:59 - Daniel: sounds good. thanks everyone.
11:03 - Aisha: thanks all, we'll follow up with the doc and schedule the perf window. bye.

Post-call notes:
- Document links shared in chat: playbook draft (link: /drive/boreal/playbooks/pilot-canary-v2), perf spreadsheet (link: /drive/boreal/perf/2025-07-loadtest.xlsx).
- Minor transcription artefacts: "dedicated" transcribed as "ded.." in places; some technical terms like KV cache appear as "K V cache" in auto text.

End of transcript.
